text:
Maya: Quick follow-up to the gateway RFC. We're seeing interaction spikes between hedging and tenant throttles that create retry storms. Need a refactor proposal.
Ben: Confirmed in yesterday's load run. Some tenants got hedged twice and exhausted their concurrency window.
Priya: The pattern: hedge -> upstream queuing -> throttle fires -> upstream rejects -> client retries -> loop. Notably noisy on small-tenant embeddings.
Javier: Proposal: separate 'hedge_budget' admission from billed concurrency quota. Hedge decisions are a soft reserve with lower priority and their own counters.
Maya: So two pools: billing_quota (strict) and hedge_quota (soft). Hedge admits won't steal billing_quota.
Ben: We should scope per-route and per-model policies. Embedding routes need tiny per-tenant hedge budgets; chat routes get larger.
Priya: Observability must include hedging tags: route/model/tenant/outcome. Current logs don't attribute hedges well.
Maya: Sketch config: 
```
edge_hedging:
  default_window_s: 60
  routes:
    - path: /v1/chat
      hedge_budget: {global: 1200, per_tenant: 8}
    - path: /v1/embeddings
      hedge_budget: {global: 300, per_tenant: 2}
```
Ben: Add adaptive thresholds: if global_util < 0.6 allow burst tranche.
Javier: Implementation constraint: token check must be local and nonblocking in the proxy. No per-request control-plane RPCs. Use local lease cache with async reconciliation.
Priya: Local cache idea: small LRU per-tenant with lease batches (e.g., allocate N tokens every T seconds). On stale reads, allow a brief grace of 1 token, then deny until refresh. Backoff on errors.
Maya: How to avoid double-alloc across proxies? Use per-proxy conservative allocation: central store issues periodic small leases; proxies spend locally. If leases run out, proxies deny hedges until lease top-up.
Ben: Accounting: hedge admits decrement local lease immediately. Billing still follows real execution start/completion. We'll reconcile leases against actual runs to avoid drift.
Priya: Failure cases: if a proxy admits a hedge but upstream cancels, we must return the used lease back or mark it reconciled. Design needs a reconciliation job that corrects lease deltas.
Javier: Race note: simultaneous admit on two proxies could oversubscribe if leases are too coarse. Keep lease batch size small (e.g., 1-3 tokens) for hot tenants. For low QPS tenants, bigger batches OK.
Maya: Rollout plan: feature flag per-cluster, default off. Enable for a handful of low-risk tenants. Monitor hedged-deny rate and tenant error spike correlation.
Ben: API signal to clients: when hedge denied, return header X-Redwood-Hedge: denied; retry-after=150ms. Encourage clients to use exponential backoff instead of immediate retry.
Priya: Observability additions: hedged_count, hedged_denied, hedged_latency_p50/90/99, hedged_error_rate, per-tenant hedge_leases_remaining gauge.
infra-bot: Canary created: edge image + hedge-cache v1 + feature-flag gate. Deploy plan: https://deploys.redwood/internal/plan/1288
Maya: Next steps: Priya write RFC addendum (schema + metrics + rollout). Javier prototype cache and lease flow. Ben add dashboard widgets and alerts.
Javier: I can spike the cache this week, will push a README and simple simulator.
Ben: I'll mock dashboards off metrics the infra-bot emits.
Priya: I'll draft the addendum and include reconciliation pseudocode.
Maya: Great. We'll review in arch sync Friday. :thumbsup:
